extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting papers to the AAAI 2023 Conference (AI/ML researchers preparing reproducibility information)
extracted.subtask_description: A conference reproducibility checklist specifying what information authors must provide (in paper or technical appendix) about methods, theory, datasets, code, and experiments to enable replication. It is intended to be completed by paper authors and appended to the technical appendix if extra explanation is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility answer guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless specified otherwise, please answer “yes” to each question if the relevant information is described either in the paper itself or in a technical appendix with an explicit reference from the main paper. If you wish to explain an answer further, please do so in a section titled “Reproducibility Checklist” at the end of the technical appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should treat information present either in the main paper or in a referenced technical appendix as satisfying checklist items. If further explanation is needed, add a clearly labeled 'Reproducibility Checklist' section at the end of the technical appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual outline or pseudocode
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes a conceptual outline and/or pseudocode description of AI methods introduced (yes/partial/no/NA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether the paper contains a high-level conceptual description and/or pseudocode for introduced methods; partial is allowed if only some methods are described. NA if not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish opinion vs facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly delineates statements that are opinions, hypothesis, and speculation from objective facts and results (yes/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should explicitly mark or write so that conjectures, hypotheses, or speculative remarks are not conflated with empirical or theoretical results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical references for replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides well marked pedagogical references for less-familiare readers to gain background necessary to replicate the paper (yes/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply references or pointers (clearly marked) to background material that would allow non-expert readers to reproduce the work; mark them clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical contributions present
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this paper make theoretical contributions? (yes/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditional question — if yes, complete the following theory-specific checklist items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory: state assumptions and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: All assumptions and restrictions are stated clearly and formally. (yes/partial/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should list formal assumptions and domain restrictions underlying theoretical results; partial indicates some but not all assumptions are formalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory: formal statement of novel claims
rubrics_metrics.description: All novel claims are stated formally (e.g., in theorem statements). (yes/partial/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel theoretical claims should be presented as formal propositions/theorems/lemmas rather than only in prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory: include proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: Proofs of all novel claims are included. (yes/partial/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full proofs (or point to appendix) for new theoretical claims; partial may indicate sketches only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory: proof sketches or intuitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof sketches or intuitions are given for complex and/or novel results. (yes/partial/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When full proofs are too long or complex, provide sketches or intuitive explanations to aid understanding and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory: cite theoretical tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate citations to theoretical tools used are given. (yes/partial/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite prior results, lemmas, or external theorems relied upon in proofs or theory development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory: empirical demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: All theoretical claims are demonstrated empirically to hold. (yes/partial/no/NA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appropriate, include experiments verifying theoretical predictions; NA if not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory: experimental code for falsification
rubrics_metrics.description: All experimental code used to eliminate or disprove claims is included. (yes/no/NA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If experiments were used to test or disprove theoretical claims, include that code or mark NA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets present
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this paper rely on one or more datasets? (yes/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditional question — if yes, answer dataset-specific items below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets: motivation for dataset choice
rubrics_metrics.description: A motivation is given for why the experiments are conducted on the selected datasets (yes/partial/no/NA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why chosen datasets are appropriate for the experiments; partial if some justification is given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets: include novel datasets in appendix
rubrics_metrics.description: All novel datasets introduced in this paper are included in a data appendix. (yes/partial/no/NA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full dataset details and data files in a data appendix for any newly created datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets: public release of novel datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: All novel datasets introduced in this paper will be made publicly available upon publication of the paper with a license that allows free usage for research purposes. (yes/partial/no/NA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to public release with an appropriate research-friendly license (or mark NA if not applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets: cite existing datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: All datasets drawn from the existing literature (potentially including authors’ own previously published work) are accompanied by appropriate citations. (yes/no/NA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide citations for any reused datasets; NA if none are reused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets: public availability of existing datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: All datasets drawn from the existing literature (potentially including authors’ own previously published work) are publicly available. (yes/partial/no/NA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether reused datasets are publicly accessible, or explain if not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets: describe non-public datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: All datasets that are not publicly available are described in detail, with explanation why publicly available alternatives are not scientifically satisficing. (yes/partial/no/NA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proprietary or private datasets, include detailed description and justification for not using public alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computational experiments present
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this paper include computational experiments? (yes/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditional question — if yes, complete the experimental reproducibility checklist below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code: preprocessing code included
rubrics_metrics.description: Any code required for pre-processing data is included in the appendix. (yes/partial/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include scripts or code snippets used to clean or preprocess data prior to experiments; partial if some preprocessing code is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code: source code included
rubrics_metrics.description: All source code required for conducting and analyzing the experiments is included in a code appendix. (yes/partial/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the experimental code used to run and analyze experiments, ideally in a code appendix or repository.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code: public release of source code
rubrics_metrics.description: All source code required for conducting and analyzing the experiments will be made publicly available upon publication of the paper with a license that allows free usage for research purposes. (yes/partial/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to releasing code under a research-friendly license upon publication, or explain restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code: comments and mapping to paper
rubrics_metrics.description: All source code implementing new methods have comments detailing the implementation, with references to the paper where each step comes from (yes/partial/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Code should be commented and cross-referenced to equations, pseudocode, or sections in the paper to ease replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomness: seed-setting described
rubrics_metrics.description: If an algorithm depends on randomness, then the method used for setting seeds is described in a way sufficient to allow replication of results. (yes/partial/no/NA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe RNG seeds, how randomness is controlled, and any non-deterministic sources; NA if not applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute infrastructure specified
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper specifies the computing infrastructure used for running experiments (hardware and software), including GPU/CPU models; amount of memory; operating system; names and versions of relevant software libraries and frameworks. (yes/partial/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List exact hardware (GPU/CPU models, memory), OS, and library/framework versions used for experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics described and motivated
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper formally describes evaluation metrics used and explains the motivation for choosing these metrics. (yes/partial/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define metrics precisely and justify why they are appropriate for the task.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of runs reported
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper states the number of algorithm runs used to compute each reported result. (yes/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how many independent runs were used to produce reported statistics (e.g., average over N seeds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analysis includes variation/confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of experiments goes beyond single-dimensional summaries of performance (e.g., average; median) to include measures of variation, confidence, or other distributional information. (yes/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include standard deviations, confidence intervals, boxplots, or other measures of variability rather than only point estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical significance testing
rubrics_metrics.description: The significance of any improvement or decrease in performance is judged using appropriate statistical tests (e.g., Wilcoxon signed-rank). (yes/partial/no)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate statistical tests to assess significance of differences; state which tests were used and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperparameters: final values listed
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper lists all final (hyper-)parameters used for each model/algorithm in the paper’s experiments. (yes/partial/no/NA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a complete table or list of final hyperparameter settings used for reported experiments; NA if none.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperparameters: search range and selection criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper states the number and range of values tried per (hyper-) parameter during development of the paper, along with the criterion used for selecting the final parameter setting. (yes/partial/no/NA)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report hyperparameter search ranges, number of trials, and selection procedure (e.g., validation metric) used to pick final settings.
